evidence.shows: Epoch estimated that Horinger in Inner Mongolia had used 11% of the cumulative Ascend 910C stock by August and identified other large Chinese data centers. This describes existing deployed stock, not the share of new chips allocated during the forecast window.

A27-024.thesis: A leading US lab releases a smaller frontier agent that costs one tenth as much as its preceding Agent-1-equivalent model.
A27-024.bar: A leading US lab releases a smaller agent at no more than one tenth the comparable cost of its preceding frontier agent. The essay does not specify the pricing unit.
A27-024.target: 10× cheaper: one tenth of the preceding model's cost
A27-024.measure: Comparable inference or access cost for the released smaller model relative to the lab's preceding frontier agent
indicatorsDecisive: Published comparable pricing or documented inference costs show a released smaller agent costs at most one tenth as much as the same lab's preceding frontier agent.
indicatorsSupporting: The lab announces public availability of a smaller agent model.
Published API price schedules show relative input and output prices.
Independent deployment estimates compare inference costs under equivalent workloads.
Model cards document the relationship between the smaller model and the preceding frontier agent.
indicatorsNo: Comparable pricing and cost evidence shows no released smaller agent from a leading US lab reaches the tenfold cost reduction against its preceding frontier agent.
A27-024.measureUsed: Standard uncached API price per million input and output tokens at release: OpenAI o4-mini cost $1.10 input and $4.40 output, versus $15 input and $60 output for the preceding frontier reasoning model o1. Both rates imply a 13.64× reduction, or 1.36 times the 10× target.
A27-024.reasoning: OpenAI released the smaller, tool-capable o4-mini after its frontier o1 model, and its standard input and output token prices were each about 13.6 times cheaper than o1’s. This meets the fixed reading’s comparable access-cost bar before the window, which the grading rules count as an early Hit. The narrower lineage comparison against o3-mini shows no price reduction, but the reading calls for comparison with a preceding frontier model, for which o1 is a defensible candidate; token prices do not establish equal total cost for every completed task.

evidence.item: OpenAI o3 and o4-mini system card
evidence.shows: Describes o4-mini as a reasoning model with full tool capabilities, supporting its use as an agent model.

evidence.item: Reporting on the o3 and o4-mini launches
evidence.shows: Reports immediate release of o4-mini and describes it as a smaller, faster model.

evidence.item: Launch pricing comparison
evidence.shows: Reports o4-mini API prices of $1.10/$4.40 per million input/output tokens and o1 prices of $15/$60; it also identifies o3-mini as the predecessor of the smaller reasoning-model line.

A27-025.thesis: The US stock market rises 30% over 2026, led by AI-related companies.
A27-025.bar: The US broad market gains 30% over the full calendar year. The essay associates the rise with AI, but does not specify whether dividends are included.
A27-025.actor: The US broad stock market; the S&P 500 is the contextual proxy.
A27-025.measure: S&P 500 price return from the end of 2025 to the end of 2026, with total return checked separately

indicatorsSupporting: S&P 500 total return for 2026.
Contribution of AI-related companies to the S&P 500's 2026 gain.
2026 earnings and investment reports for major AI-related companies.
indicatorsNo: Both S&P 500 price and total returns for calendar 2026 fall below 30%.
A27-025.measureUsed: S&P 500 price return from the December 31, 2025 close of 6,845.50 to the November 23, 2026 close of 7,237.17: approximately 5.72%, or 0.191 of the 30% target. The separately checked total return was 8.78% year to date through November 6; a comparable November 23 total-return figure was not verified.
A27-025.reasoning: The S&P 500 price index was up approximately 5.72% as of November 23, well below the 30% full-year target. It would need to end 2026 at or above 8,899.15, a further gain of approximately 23% from that close, so the trajectory is off track with a little over a month remaining. The latest verified total-return comparison is earlier and also below the target; the calendar-year outcome remains open.

evidence.item: S&P 500 year-end close
evidence.shows: The index closed 2025 at 6,845.50, establishing the baseline.

evidence.item: S&P 500 daily close and year-to-date change
evidence.shows: The index closed at 7,237.17, up 391.67 points or 5.7% for 2026.

evidence.item: S&P 500 year-to-date total return
evidence.shows: The S&P 500 total return, including dividends, was 8.78% through November 6, below 30%; this is an earlier date than the latest price-return observation.

evidence.item: AI-related stocks and the market rebound
evidence.shows: Nvidia shares rose 31.5% on November 23, and the company was among the most influential constituents of the index. This supports the relevance of AI-related companies, though it does not establish their contribution to the full-year gain.

A27-026.thesis: AI disrupts the US junior software-engineering job market.
A27-026.bar: By late 2026, credible evidence shows substantial disruption in the US market for junior software engineers associated with AI. The text does not specify a numerical employment change.
A27-026.actor: US employers and workers in the junior software-engineering labor market.
indicatorsDecisive: A comprehensive labor-market study combining employment, hiring and employer evidence finds substantial AI-linked disruption to US junior software-engineering work by late 2026.
indicatorsSupporting: BLS CPS and CES employment trends for software developers, supplemented by age or experience breakdowns.
Indeed Hiring Lab postings for entry-level software roles.
CRA Taulbee or National Student Clearinghouse computing enrollment and graduate trends.
Employer surveys and wage data on junior engineering hiring and AI use.
indicatorsNo: Employment, hiring, vacancies and wages show a stable junior software-engineering market through late 2026, with no credible evidence of substantial AI-linked disruption.
A27-026.measureUsed: No numerical target. Assessed US junior software-engineering hiring and work using developer vacancy comparisons, employer and worker reporting, payroll evidence for young workers, and research on firms adopting AI coding tools. The estimates describe different populations and should not be added together.
A27-026.reasoning: By September, reporting on employers and graduates, together with the national software-vacancy study and broader labor-market evidence, supported substantial disruption associated with AI; the later procurement-cycle study strengthens the causal case. The contrary studies are consequential: their broader occupation groups or observational adopter comparisons measure different populations and relationships, so they do not negate the more targeted evidence, although the size of AI's market-wide contribution remains uncertain. The bar does not require an overall decline in software employment or proof that AI can perform everything taught in a CS degree.

evidence.item: AP reporting on computer science graduates and entry-level hiring
evidence.shows: Reports a difficult entry-level market and employer demands for more experienced workers able to oversee AI tools. It also reports that employment of young workers across highly AI-exposed occupations was 19% below a comparison trajectory; that figure is not specific to software engineers.

evidence.item: Study of US online software vacancies
evidence.shows: Finds a 14–15% relative decline in junior versus senior software-developer vacancies after ChatGPT's release, alongside increased experience requirements within job titles. The comparison associates the change with generative AI but does not by itself establish causation.

evidence.item: AI-Assisted Programming and Labor Demand
evidence.shows: A study of 5,414 multinational firms uses procurement cycles to address selection into Copilot adoption. Among firms induced to adopt by procurement reviews, quarterly technical hiring was 29% lower after one year, concentrated in highly code-intensive junior roles; overall technical headcount and separations did not significantly change.

evidence.item: Federal Reserve analysis of CPS coder employment
evidence.shows: Coder employment continued to grow, but growth slowed sharply after ChatGPT's introduction even after an adjustment for industry-level shocks. The analysis covers coders generally and does not establish an AI cause or a junior-specific effect.

evidence.item: New York Fed study of vacancies in AI-exposed occupations
evidence.shows: Finds that the relative decline in vacancies began before ChatGPT and that junior and senior postings in highly exposed occupations moved broadly in parallel, challenging a general AI-driven entry-level explanation.
evidence.source: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

evidence.item: Peer-reviewed study of Copilot adoption and software-engineer hiring
evidence.shows: Finds adoption associated with a 3–5% higher monthly probability of hiring software engineers, driven by entry-level hires. This observational association differs from the later procurement-cycle study's estimate for firms induced to adopt.

Organizer attendance estimates and documented mobilization.

Lab or DOD announcements of operational AI partnerships.

evidence.shows: The contract covers identifying and prototyping frontier AI applications, including work with program and acquisition data and proactive cyber defense.

A27-029.thesis: The worldwide active stock of AI compute has a cost of ownership of $1 trillion in 2026.
A27-029.bar: The cost of ownership of the active worldwide AI-relevant compute stock reaches $1 trillion in 2026. This is a stock cost, not annual capex.
A27-029.measure: Cost of ownership of the active global stock of AI-relevant compute, including associated data-center infrastructure
indicatorsDecisive: An Epoch AI or comparable global inventory, valued using documented hardware and associated infrastructure ownership costs, estimates at least $1 trillion for active AI-relevant compute in 2026.
indicatorsSupporting: Nvidia, AMD and other accelerator supplier shipments and pricing in company filings.
Hyperscaler and lab capital-expenditure filings.
Epoch AI and SemiAnalysis data-center inventories and capacity estimates.
indicatorsNo: A comprehensive 2026 global active-stock valuation using the essay's scope is materially below $1 trillion.
A27-029.measureUsed: Cost of ownership of the active worldwide stock of AI-relevant compute, including associated data-center infrastructure. No sufficiently supported 2026 valuation on this measure was found. Annual spending, shipments, and potential data-center capacity are supporting indicators, not valuations of the active stock.
A27-029.reasoning: The spending and shipment evidence shows a large, rapidly growing buildout, but it does not establish a defensible value for the active global stock including its associated infrastructure. I checked Epoch AI’s chip and data-center inventories, searched for accessible SemiAnalysis estimates, and examined company, IEA and analyst evidence; none of the figures found resolves the stock valuation or supports a reliable ratio to $1 trillion. The window remains open, but without a sufficiently supported current stock estimate, both whether the target has already been reached and the trajectory are unclear. A global inventory that values active qualifying equipment and its associated infrastructure would settle the test.

evidence.item: Epoch AI data-center inventory
evidence.shows: Epoch estimates that its inventory covers 43% of global deployed AI computing capacity, with a 90% confidence interval of 29%–77%. That coverage is measured in compute capacity and cannot by itself establish the ownership cost of the worldwide active stock.

evidence.item: Epoch AI chip-sales dataset
evidence.shows: The dataset estimates sales and shipments, computing power, cost, and power draw of leading AI chips using company and analyst data. Shipments and chip costs alone do not establish which equipment is active or the ownership cost of associated infrastructure.

evidence.item: NVIDIA fiscal 2027 third-quarter results
evidence.shows: NVIDIA reported $107.6 billion in data-center revenue for the quarter ended October 25, 2026. This is evidence of substantial equipment sales, but company revenue is not a global active-stock valuation.

evidence.item: World Energy Outlook 2026
evidence.shows: The IEA inferred 17 GW of potential capacity at 93 purpose-built AI data centers from operational real estate as of September 2026. This is neither a comprehensive inventory of active compute nor a valuation.

evidence.item: Worldwide quarterly AI infrastructure tracker
evidence.shows: IDC reports $121.4 billion in AI infrastructure spending in Q2 2026. This measures quarterly server and storage spending rather than the value of the active worldwide stock including facilities.

evidence.item: AI data-center supply and demand outlook
evidence.shows: BCG estimates that five hyperscalers are on track to allot over $800 billion to data-center capex in 2026, while supply-chain constraints hold back capacity. The spending includes buildout and is not a valuation of assets already active.

A27-030.thesis: Global AI infrastructure has 38 GW of peak power requirement in 2026.
A27-030.bar: Worldwide AI-relevant compute and its data-center infrastructure require at least 38 GW at peak in 2026.
A27-030.measure: Aggregate peak data-center power requirement for worldwide AI-relevant compute
indicatorsDecisive: An IEA or comparable worldwide inventory of AI-specific data-center peak power requirements estimates at least 38 GW in 2026.
indicatorsSupporting: Epoch AI and SemiAnalysis inventories of AI data-center capacity.
Operator and utility filings on energized AI data-center loads.
Accelerator shipments combined with chip and facility power specifications.
indicatorsNo: A comprehensive AI-specific global peak-power inventory finds materially less than 38 GW in 2026.
A27-030.measureUsed: Estimated aggregate peak facility power for AI-relevant compute, including supporting infrastructure. A reconstruction using Epoch AI chip-sales data and its facility-power method estimates 39.4 GW in Q1 2026. TrendForce separately estimates 53.8 GW of global AI-server power demand capacity for 2026.
A27-030.reasoning: The best available triangulation puts worldwide AI-related peak facility requirements above 38 GW during 2026: the Epoch-based Q1 estimate is 39.4 GW, or about 1.04 times the target, and TrendForce's independent annual estimate is higher. The Q1 figure is close to the threshold and depends on chip-sales and facility-overhead assumptions; it is not a direct inventory of energized load. The IEA's 17 GW figure covers only 93 large purpose-built sites, so its narrower scope does not contradict the worldwide estimates. The resolution date records the end of the first quarter in which the threshold is estimated to have been met, not a known exact day.

evidence.item: Global AI power capacity is now comparable to peak power usage of New York State
evidence.shows: Epoch AI estimates approximately 30 GW of global AI data-center peak power capacity in Q4 2025. It multiplies sold chips' rated power by 2.5 to include servers, networking, cooling and other facility needs; it identifies uncertainty in the multiplier and extrapolated sales.

evidence.item: AI data centre power capacity reached 39.4 GW by Q1 2026
evidence.shows: Using Epoch AI's chip-sales data and the same 2.5 facility multiplier, the reconstruction estimates 15.7 GW of rated chip power and 39.4 GW including infrastructure in Q1 2026. This is an estimated peak requirement, not a measurement of actual electricity consumption.

evidence.item: AI Servers Now Set the Data Center Power Budget
evidence.shows: TrendForce's server-shipment-based analysis estimates global AI-server power demand capacity at 53.8 GW in 2026. This independently supports the scale, although demand capacity and energized, deployed load need not be identical.

evidence.item: World Energy Outlook 2026
evidence.shows: The IEA estimates 17 GW of potential capacity associated with operational real estate at 93 large purpose-built AI data centers as of September. This is a partial-site inventory, not an estimate of all worldwide AI-relevant compute, and therefore does not establish a global total below 38 GW.

A27-031.thesis: A leading US AI lab earns $45 billion in annual AI revenue in 2026.
A27-031.bar: A leading US AI lab earns at least $45 billion in AI revenue during 2026. The tracker says $35 billion, but the supplied main panel and compute supplement both say $45 billion; the discrepancy should be preserved rather than silently substituting the tracker number.
A27-031.actor: Any leading US AI lab; for a diversified company, its AI activities.
