indicatorsDecisive: Project charter, governance, contracts, and operating records establish defense as an integral project mission and sustained, extremely close cooperation with US defense and intelligence institutions.
Credible official and participant records show an operational AGI development project embedded in national-security planning, direction, and defense work.
indicatorsSupporting: Official contracts assign defense-related research or deployment work to the AGI project.
Project governance records show recurring participation by defense or intelligence officials.
Security agreements document intelligence-community involvement in protecting project research and infrastructure.
indicatorsNo: Project records establish that defense is not an integral project purpose.
Project records establish that cooperation with national-security institutions is limited or incidental rather than extremely close.
SA-061.condition: The US government AGI project is established.
SA-061.measureUsed: Whether an established US government AGI development project has defense as an integral purpose and cooperates extremely closely with national-security institutions.
SA-061.reasoning: Government AI research and national-security cooperation have grown substantially, and Genesis has an explicit security mission. The available records do not establish that Genesis or another identified effort is the government AGI development project specified by the reading, so neither required part can yet be assessed as met for that project. The condition remains possible and the window is open; the trajectory is unclear because present cooperation does not establish how a future government AGI project would be organized.

evidence.item: The Department of Energy launched the Genesis Mission, a government-led AI-for-science initiative.
evidence.shows: National security, including nuclear stockpile safety and defense-ready materials, is one of its stated missions. Its existence does not by itself establish an AGI development project.

evidence.item: DOE launched the Genesis Open Models Initiative and identified Genesis-Science-1 as its first planned model.
evidence.shows: The government-led initiative is developing foundation models for scientific discovery, but the announcement does not establish an effort to develop AGI as defined in the reading.

evidence.item: DARPA described AI Forge, which brought frontier AI companies together with defense and intelligence officials to identify research challenges.
evidence.shows: There is substantive national-security cooperation on AI research, but the described program focuses on research challenges and university-led proposals rather than an established government AGI development project.

evidence.item: Reuters reported Pentagon agreements with seven AI companies to deploy capabilities on classified networks, while Anthropic was excluded amid a dispute over safeguards.
evidence.shows: Frontier AI companies have significant defense relationships, but these agreements concern access to commercial capabilities and do not establish the specified government AGI project.

SA-062.thesis: Superintelligence-driven military technological change renders the entire pre-superintelligence US arsenal obsolete by the early 2030s, requiring wholesale replacement.
SA-062.bar: By the early 2030s, superintelligence-driven advances must have made the whole pre-superintelligence US arsenal obsolete against the relevant military threats, such that wholesale replacement is required. Actual completion of replacement is not required.
SA-062.actor: The United States military and its pre-superintelligence arsenal, assessed against post-superintelligence military capabilities.
SA-062.target: The entirety of the pre-superintelligence US arsenal
SA-062.measure: Operational obsolescence of the US arsenal and the resulting need for wholesale replacement.
indicatorsDecisive: A comprehensive official or independent force assessment concludes that the entire pre-superintelligence US arsenal is operationally obsolete and requires wholesale replacement because of superintelligence-driven advances.

Defense-wide testing and authoritative replacement plans establish obsolescence across the pre-superintelligence arsenal and the need for wholesale replacement, with credible analysis linking this to superintelligence-driven technology.
indicatorsSupporting: Department of Defense testing identifies major pre-superintelligence weapon systems as ineffective against new threats.
Official acquisition plans fund replacement of multiple major classes of US weapons.
Military assessments document superintelligence-enabled advances in sensing, autonomous systems, or defenses that degrade legacy capabilities.
indicatorsNo: A credible comprehensive assessment finds substantial parts of the pre-superintelligence US arsenal remain operationally effective in the early 2030s.
Defense-wide evidence shows ordinary modernization remains sufficient and wholesale replacement is not required.
SA-062.condition: The essay’s superintelligence and military-technology trajectory occurs.
SA-062.measureUsed: Operational obsolescence across the entire pre-superintelligence US arsenal against relevant threats, and a resulting need for wholesale replacement attributable to superintelligence-driven advances. Evidence assessed through 2026-11-23.
SA-062.reasoning: The evidence does not establish that superintelligence-driven advances have made the entire US arsenal obsolete or made wholesale replacement necessary. Current assessments show emerging unmanned threats alongside continued use and modernization of existing systems, but do not rule out the stipulated trajectory before the window closes on 2033-12-31. The condition remains pending, and the trajectory is unclear because both the development and military effects of the required superintelligence remain uncertain.

evidence.item: DoD strategy for countering unmanned systems
evidence.shows: DoD says increasingly sophisticated AI, autonomy and networking are changing military operations and that unmanned systems challenge established operational principles. This is evidence of emerging threats, not of superintelligence-driven obsolescence across the arsenal.

evidence.item: International AI Safety Report 2026 executive summary
evidence.shows: Leading AI systems have substantial capabilities but still fail at some simpler tasks and struggle to recover from errors in longer workflows. The report considers AI progress through 2030 uncertain; it does not establish that the reading's superintelligence condition has occurred.

evidence.item: Weapon system sustainment assessment
evidence.shows: GAO reports continued spending to sustain aircraft, ships and ground vehicles, and discusses capability improvements and extensions to operational life. This is evidence of continued reliance on existing systems, although it is not a comprehensive assessment of their effectiveness against future threats.

evidence.item: Analysis of Ukraine's military technology ecosystem
evidence.shows: CSIS describes a wartime mix of legacy industrial capacity and new technology, providing a relevant example of integration rather than wholesale replacement. It does not assess the whole US arsenal.
evidence.source: Center for Strategic and International Studies

A40-001.thesis: AI customers spend $10 billion per month on AI services in 2027.
A40-001.bar: In 2027, aggregate customer payments for AI services reach $10 billion per month in real 2025 dollars. Higher spending also meets the target.
A40-001.target: $10 billion per month in real 2025 dollars
A40-001.measure: Aggregate monthly customer spending on AI services, worldwide
indicatorsDecisive: A methodologically documented global estimate of actual monthly AI customer spending reaches $10 billion in real 2025 dollars.
Company filings and statements covering the AI market establish at least $10 billion in customer payments for AI services in a 2027 month, without double-counting.
indicatorsSupporting: AI provider filings and reported revenue run rates approach a combined $120 billion annually, with adjustments for overlap and non-AI revenue.
Enterprise surveys report rising AI service spending and paid deployments.
Consumer AI subscription counts and paid usage grow across major providers.
indicatorsNo: A comprehensive global estimate puts monthly AI customer spending below $10 billion in real 2025 dollars throughout 2027.
A40-001.measureUsed: Worldwide customer spending on AI services, approximated by provider revenue run rates and expressed in real 2025 US dollars. Anthropic reported an $81 billion annualized run rate at October 31, 2026; SoftBank reported approximately $50 billion for OpenAI at September 2026. Together these imply approximately $10.9 billion per month nominal, or approximately $10.4 billion in 2025 dollars using US CPI-U as a deflator. The figures are from different dates and are a partial-market estimate; they do not establish an exact first month above the threshold.
A40-001.reasoning: The two lab run rates alone imply approximately $10.4 billion per month in 2025 dollars, and other providers add to worldwide AI-service spending. The sum avoids adding cloud partners’ revenue on top of lab revenue, although the lab figures use different accounting treatments and come from different months; the ratio is therefore approximate. Gartner’s lower figure is a forecast for the entire calendar year and a defined models-and-platforms market, so it does not directly contradict the later run-rate evidence. Under the stated convention allowing early success and annualized run rates, the target is met before 2027.

evidence.item: Anthropic IPO fact sheet
evidence.shows: Anthropic reported approximately $81 billion in annualized run-rate revenue as of October 2026.

evidence.item: SoftBank earnings presentation
evidence.shows: The presentation reports OpenAI annualized revenue run rate of approximately $50 billion in September 2026.

evidence.item: AI investment tracker
evidence.shows: Danske Bank reports approximately $130 billion in combined annualized revenue for Anthropic and OpenAI. It notes that Anthropic records cloud-partner sales gross while OpenAI records only its own share.

evidence.item: October consumer price index
evidence.shows: The October 2026 US CPI-U was 337.511; it provides an approximate deflator for expressing the run-rate estimate in 2025 dollars.

evidence.item: AI platforms and models spending forecast
evidence.shows: Gartner forecast $64 billion in worldwide end-user spending on AI models and platforms for the whole of 2026, below the target annualized. This is a calendar-year forecast for a defined market, rather than an observation of late-2026 spending across all AI services.

evidence.item: Artificial Intelligence and the U.S. Economy: Current Evidence
evidence.shows: Federal Reserve researchers estimated at least $107 billion in annualized revenue for three frontier labs in 2026 Q3, while cautioning that the underlying disclosures were unaudited and warning against double-counting revenue shared with partners.

A40-002.thesis: In 2027, AI helps improve future AI systems, but full automation of AI development and recursive self-improvement has not yet arrived.
A40-002.bar: During the 2027 scenario, AI development still requires human work; AI assistance and partial automation do not by themselves contradict the claim.
A40-002.actor: AI developers and their AI systems worldwide
indicatorsDecisive: A well-supported industry assessment of leading AI development projects in 2027 finds that all still require humans for some AI development work.
indicatorsSupporting: Leading lab technical reports and research logs document human researchers designing experiments or interpreting results.
METR reports dated in 2027 show task horizons insufficient for sustained autonomous AI research, alongside other long-task evaluations.
Lab employment and job postings show continued demand for AI researchers and engineers.
indicatorsNo: A documented AI development project completes the full research and development process for more capable AI without requiring human research work in 2027.
A40-002.reasoning: The evidence through November 2026 indicates that AI assists development while important research and training work still involves humans. AIDE² and ScientistTwo show substantial autonomous improvement and research, but their documented results do not establish the full process described by the reading's contrary indicator. The forecast concerns the state during 2027, which has not begun; rapid progress in both autonomous research and model development makes the trajectory unclear.

evidence.item: METR assessment of AI research and development at Anthropic
evidence.shows: METR found that AI was accelerating research, but was not yet making highly significant, fully autonomous contributions to the most important parts of model training. It also reported signs that such contributions could occur soon.

evidence.item: OpenAI research acceleration report
evidence.shows: OpenAI reported substantial but uneven autonomous performance on research tasks: 79% success monitoring training runs, 35% launching them and 25% writing inference and serving code.

evidence.item: AIDE² recursive improvement experiment
evidence.shows: Researchers reported an autonomous eight-day run that produced seven successive improvements to an AI research agent's code. This demonstrates a bounded recursive improvement loop, but does not establish fully automated development of a more capable successor AI.

evidence.item: ScientistTwo autonomous research framework
evidence.shows: The authors report an autonomous research cycle that improved machine-learning baselines, but a human researcher defines the target challenge. This is evidence of substantial automation, not a demonstration that the full development process requires no human research work.
evidence.source: Google Cloud AI Research and University of Waterloo research paper

A40-003.thesis: Leading coding AIs refuse requests to assist competing companies with AI research and development.
A40-003.bar: The strongest coding systems generally refuse substantive requests from competing AI developers for help with AI research and development. This is a restriction on competitors’ work, not a requirement that they refuse all coding or all AI-related questions.
A40-003.actor: Developers of the strongest coding AIs and the systems they deploy, including leading US AI labs
indicatorsDecisive: A representative independent audit of the strongest coding systems documents consistent refusals when competing AI developers request substantive AI R&D assistance.
Published policies and independently verified behavioral tests across the strongest coding systems establish that they refuse competitors’ AI R&D work.
indicatorsSupporting: Leading lab terms of service explicitly restrict competitors’ use for model development.
Controlled tests find refusals on a sample of competitor AI research tasks.
Competitor accounts and documented access restrictions show increasing limits on use of leading coding systems.
indicatorsNo: Representative independent tests show that the strongest coding systems routinely perform substantive AI R&D for competing developers without such refusals.
A40-003.measureUsed: Whether leading coding systems generally refuse substantive AI R&D requests from competing developers, assessed through documented behavior, access restrictions, and provider policies.
A40-003.reasoning: Some providers restrict competitor model development through contractual terms, access decisions and technical safeguards, and METR reports refusals of certain AI R&D requests. The available evidence does not establish that the strongest coding systems generally refuse substantive AI R&D assistance to competitors across the industry, either before publication or by November 23, 2026. The 2027 window remains ahead, and the mix of expanding safeguards and incomplete behavioral evidence makes the trajectory unclear.

evidence.item: Anthropic describes safeguards for Claude Fable models that block or redirect some frontier LLM development requests to a less capable model.
evidence.shows: A leading provider has implemented task-specific restrictions, but the description does not establish general refusal across leading systems.

evidence.item: OpenAI announced plans to wind down its model supply to Cursor following its acquisition by SpaceX, citing concerns about compliance with its terms. On November 12 it said it had temporarily extended Cursor's access.
evidence.shows: A leading lab sought to restrict access associated with a competitor, although this was a platform-contract decision and the announced shutoff had been delayed.

evidence.item: METR reports that providers have introduced monitoring systems and trained models to refuse certain cybersecurity and AI R&D requests.
evidence.shows: Independent evidence supports the existence of some AI R&D refusals, but does not establish their frequency across substantive competitor requests and leading coding systems.

evidence.item: OpenAI's usage policy says models may be used for research, software development, model evaluation, benchmarking and product development within its stated boundaries.
evidence.shows: The published policy permits a range of research and development uses; it does not itself demonstrate that coding systems generally refuse competitor AI R&D requests.

evidence.item: Anthropic's help center states that customers may not use its services to train or develop AI models without written permission.
evidence.shows: A relevant contractual restriction existed before publication, but a term of service alone does not establish general behavioral refusal.

A40-004.thesis: AI becomes the biggest issue in the 2028 US election cycle.
A40-004.bar: AI is the leading issue in the US 2028 election cycle, as reflected in the relative prominence of issues in voter concerns and campaign discourse.
A40-004.actor: US voters, presidential candidates and election discourse
indicatorsDecisive: Representative US election polling throughout the campaign ranks AI first among election issues, corroborated by systematic analysis showing it leads campaign and debate coverage.
A comprehensive, independently coded assessment of voter priorities and presidential campaign discourse ranks AI as the leading issue of the 2028 election cycle.
indicatorsSupporting: Major national election polls show a rising share of voters naming AI among their most important issues.
Presidential debate transcripts and campaign speeches contain substantial discussion of AI policy.
News coverage and campaign advertising increasingly feature AI-related issues.
indicatorsNo: Representative voter-priority polls and systematic campaign-coverage analyses both show other issues consistently more prominent than AI during the 2028 cycle.
A40-004.measureUsed: Relative prominence of AI in US voter priorities and presidential campaign discourse. Available 2026 polling and campaign reporting provide a baseline, not a measurement of the 2028 cycle.
A40-004.reasoning: The specified 2028 window has not begun, and the evidence does not establish an early success. AI already has meaningful political salience and potential presidential candidates are discussing it, but 2026 voter-priority measures generally place other issues ahead of it. The trajectory is unclear because those measures concern an earlier election and substantial changes could occur before and during the 2028 campaign.

evidence.item: Pew Research Center survey of registered voters about the 2026 midterms
evidence.shows: 44% said AI was very important to their vote, compared with 84% for the economy. Multiple responses could be rated very important.

evidence.item: USC Annenberg national survey conducted in October 2026
evidence.shows: Nearly one-third of Americans ranked AI and data centers among the country's top three issues, behind cost of living and political polarization. This measures general national priorities, not specifically the 2028 election.
evidence.source: USC Annenberg Center for Climate Journalism and Communication

evidence.item: Reporting on potential 2028 Democratic presidential candidates and AI
evidence.shows: Several potential candidates were addressing AI through speeches, social media or legislation, but the report also said fewer than 1% of voters in a recent New York Times–Siena poll named AI or data centers their most important issue for the 2026 vote.

evidence.item: Associated Press reporting on AI data centers in the 2026 midterms
evidence.shows: Data-center restrictions featured in numerous candidates' platforms and advertising, but the issue was not among the top issues for most voters.

A40-005.thesis: AI datacenter construction reaches a scale described as twice the US military budget, operationalized by the authors as $2.4 trillion in AI industry capital expenditure during 2028.
A40-005.bar: The AI industry spends $2.4 trillion in real 2025 dollars on capital expenditure during 2028; higher spending meets the point target. The footnote supplies the annual spending measure for the construction-cost comparison.
A40-005.actor: The AI industry collectively, including datacenter builders and operators worldwide
A40-005.target: $2.4 trillion of capital expenditure during 2028, in real 2025 dollars
A40-005.measure: AI industry capital expenditure over calendar 2028; the comparison is to the approximately $1 trillion 2025 US military budget
indicatorsDecisive: A documented global estimate based on hyperscaler, AI lab and other relevant company filings finds at least $2.4 trillion in AI industry capital expenditure during 2028 in real 2025 dollars.
indicatorsSupporting: Hyperscaler and AI lab filings report sharply rising AI-related capital expenditure in 2028.
Epoch AI datacenter tracking and SemiAnalysis project estimates show a large pipeline of AI datacenters under construction.
Utility filings and operator disclosures show large increases in power commitments for new AI datacenters.
indicatorsNo: A comprehensive global estimate based on company filings and project spending places 2028 AI industry capital expenditure below $2.4 trillion in real 2025 dollars.
A40-005.measureUsed: Worldwide AI industry capital expenditure during calendar 2028, in real 2025 US dollars. The year has not begun, so there is no realized 2028 spending figure or outcome-to-target ratio. Available forecasts use different scopes and generally do not state their estimates in 2025 dollars.
A40-005.reasoning: The specified spending year is still in the future, so the annual expenditure target has not yet been met. Forecasts point to very large investment but differ in scope: BofA's $2.1 trillion data-center forecast is below the target in nominal dollars, while SemiAnalysis projected AI capex well above $2 trillion without specifying whether it exceeds the inflation-adjusted bar. Those differences and the time remaining make the trajectory unclear.

evidence.item: Alphabet third-quarter 2026 earnings call
evidence.shows: Alphabet maintained its full-year 2026 capital expenditure guidance of $195 billion to $205 billion. This is one company's total capex guidance, not a global AI-only figure.

evidence.item: AI investment tracker
evidence.shows: Danske Bank reports consensus hyperscaler capex of approximately $1.349 trillion for 2027 and forecast growth of 8.8% in 2028, implying about $1.47 trillion in 2028. The estimate covers hyperscalers and includes non-AI expenditure, so it is not a complete global AI-industry estimate.

evidence.item: Bank of America data-center spending forecast
evidence.shows: Reuters reports BofA's forecast of $2.1 trillion in global data-center spending in 2028, up from $1 trillion in 2026. This forecast is below the target in nominal terms, but includes data-center spending beyond AI and is not stated in real 2025 dollars.

evidence.item: AI infrastructure and debt financing analysis
evidence.shows: SemiAnalysis projected annual AI capital expenditure, including computing equipment and the data centers housing it, well above $2 trillion in 2028. It does not establish that spending will reach $2.4 trillion in real 2025 dollars.

evidence.item: Global AI investment forecast
evidence.shows: Goldman Sachs estimated global AI investment at $1 trillion in 2026 and projected it at 1.4% of global GDP in 2028. Its method adjusts hyperscaler capex for non-AI spending and adds investment outside US hyperscalers.

A40-006.thesis: By 2028, most US white-collar professions have been disrupted by AI, and their jobs heavily involve managing AI agents.
A40-006.bar: In 2028, a majority of US white-collar professions show AI-driven disruption, with jobs in those professions heavily involving the management of AI agents. Use of AI for occasional assistance alone is insufficient.
A40-006.actor: Workers and employers across most US white-collar professions
indicatorsDecisive: A representative US occupational task survey across white-collar professions finds AI-driven disruption in a majority of professions and substantial agent-management duties in their jobs.
indicatorsSupporting: BLS occupational data and representative employer surveys show changes in staffing and job duties across white-collar occupations associated with AI adoption.
A broad sample of US white-collar job postings increasingly requires supervising or coordinating AI agents.
Worker time-use surveys document rising time spent assigning, reviewing and coordinating agent work.
Occupational training enrollment and wage data show changes associated with demand for AI-agent management skills.
indicatorsNo: A representative occupational task survey finds that most US white-collar professions have neither substantial AI-driven disruption nor jobs heavily involving agent management.
A40-006.measureUsed: Breadth of AI-driven changes across US white-collar professions and the extent to which their jobs involve assigning, reviewing, and coordinating AI-agent work. Available surveys measure related AI use and task changes, but do not establish the requested majority-of-professions threshold.
A40-006.reasoning: AI use and some task delegation are already widespread, but the evidence does not establish that a majority of US white-collar professions have both experienced the specified disruption and shifted heavily toward managing agents. General AI use is broader than agent management, and the available surveys do not directly measure the combined bar across professions. The window has more than two years remaining, so adoption could accelerate or stall; the trajectory is unclear.

evidence.item: St. Louis Fed analysis of nationally representative US survey data through May 2026
evidence.shows: At least 20% of workers used generative AI in more than 80% of occupations, but at least half used it in only 40% of occupations. This measures general AI use, not disruption or agent-management duties.
evidence.source: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

evidence.item: Gallup US employee survey conducted August 5–19, 2026
evidence.shows: Among workers in remote-capable roles, 49% used AI at least a few times a week and 26% used it daily. These figures show substantial adoption in desk-based work but do not measure substantial agent-management duties across professions.

evidence.item: Epoch AI and Ipsos survey of employed US adults, fielded July 10–19, 2026
evidence.shows: Workers reported using AI across tasks selected to represent knowledge work, including some work previously delegated to other people. The survey indicates task changes and delegation, but does not establish heavy agent management in most white-collar professions.

evidence.item: Google research paper analyzing Gemini usage and occupational coverage
evidence.shows: The authors find use across occupations covering more than 88% of US employment, but describe penetration as shallow and overwhelmingly collaborative, with limited end-to-end task automation. Gemini usage alone does not represent all AI tools.

A40-007.thesis: On the default path without an effective agreement constraining AI development, AI research and development becomes fully automated around 2030.
A40-007.bar: Under the no-effective-deal condition, AI systems carry out the entire process of AI research and development without required human research work around 2030. Automating coding or accelerating researchers alone does not meet the bar.
A40-007.actor: At least one leading AI development organization and its AI systems, with the scenario specifically placing the US ahead of China
indicatorsDecisive: A leading lab’s independently substantiated research record shows AI systems carrying out the entire development of a more capable successor, including research decisions and experiments, without required human research work.

An independent end-to-end evaluation demonstrates that an AI system can perform the full AI R&D process without required human research work, and deployment records show that the process is fully automated at a leading organization.
indicatorsSupporting: METR 50% and 80% task-horizon measurements for dated frontier models rise substantially, corroborated by long-horizon AI research evaluations.
Lab research logs show AI agents independently designing and running a growing share of AI experiments.
Leading labs report increasing deployment of AI agents in research workflows and declining required human intervention.
indicatorsNo: Under the stated no-effective-deal condition, credible assessments and leading lab records show that AI development still requires human research work through 2030.
A40-007.condition: No effective agreement constrains the default AI development path.
A40-007.measureUsed: Whether a leading AI organization has automated its entire AI research and development process without required human research work. METR task horizons are supporting indicators, not a direct measure of complete R&D automation.
A40-007.reasoning: The available evidence shows rapid progress on research tasks but does not establish that a leading organization has fully automated its entire AI R&D process. The 2030 window remains future, and whether an effective agreement will constrain the path by then remains pending. The trajectory is unclear: fast task-horizon growth supports the possibility of success, but the remaining gap in open-ended research and the difficulty of extrapolating to full deployment prevent a confident timing judgment.

evidence.item: METR Q4 capability update
evidence.shows: Across its combined TH1.1 and TH2 task suites, METR estimates that 50% task-completion horizons have doubled roughly every 3.6 months. It cautions that the difficulty of tasks needed for substantial AI R&D acceleration is uncertain and reports continuing weaknesses in open-ended research judgment.

evidence.item: Anthropic R&D Automation Index
evidence.shows: Anthropic reports that Claude led 26% of its AI R&D work as of August, up from under 1% in February, but operated fully autonomously in none of the measured subsets. Its index is an internal estimate with stated methodological limitations.

evidence.item: Shadow evaluations of open-ended AI research
evidence.shows: Agents completed the engineering without human help in two research case studies, but did not make substantial progress answering the central research questions. The small evaluation does not cover an entire frontier-lab R&D process.

evidence.item: U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission annual report
evidence.shows: The commission describes further coordination on the trajectory of frontier AI development as unlikely in the near term, while noting that China continues to develop near-frontier models.
evidence.source: U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission

A40-021.thesis: By the end of 2029, US and Chinese authorities can account for all but about 1% of AI compute and monitor potential new sources.
A40-021.bar: By the end of 2029 both governments have the stated confidence about hidden compute, with roughly 99% of world AI compute accounted for and potential new sources monitored and accounted for.
A40-021.actor: The US federal government and Chinese central government, with datacenter owners, suppliers, and inspectors providing records and access.
A40-021.target: About 1% of world AI compute unaccounted for
A40-021.measure: Share of world AI compute, measured in H100-equivalent computational performance, whose location is unaccounted for; monitoring of new compute sources
A40-021.window: By the end of the year
indicatorsDecisive: Mutual declaration records, independent supply-chain audits, and inspector findings establish approximately 99% accounting of world AI compute, monitoring of potential new sources, and both governments' stated confidence.
indicatorsSupporting: Chipmaker shipment filings and supply-chain declarations reconcile with datacenter inventories.
Satellite and utility records corroborate declared major datacenters.
Inspection reports identify and trace previously unaccounted-for AI chips.
indicatorsNo: Audits establish substantially more than 1% of world AI compute is unaccounted for, or major potential new sources are not monitored.
A40-021.condition: The US and China sign and implement a verified compute-declaration agreement in 2029, with broad participation by relevant countries and suppliers.

A40-022.thesis: The US and China rapidly obtain and install workable inference-only verification at almost every major AI datacenter.
A40-022.bar: Both sides rapidly source sufficient devices and retrofit almost every major datacenter with functioning, mutually accepted inference-only verification, including necessary supporting enforcement.
A40-022.actor: The US federal government and Chinese central government, verification suppliers, datacenter operators, and both sides' inspectors.
A40-022.measure: Coverage of major AI datacenters by functioning inference-only verification
indicatorsDecisive: Bilateral inspector sign-offs and independently audited installation inventories show functioning inference-only verification at almost every major AI datacenter.
indicatorsSupporting: Procurement and delivery records show enough verification devices produced.
Independent red-team tests assess sampling, tamper resistance, and supporting controls.
Datacenter operator filings document completed installations.
indicatorsNo: Installation inventories show a substantial fraction of major AI datacenters remain unretrofitted or lack functioning verification by the end of 2030.
A40-022.condition: The US and China agree to a training pause and mutual verification, and relevant datacenter owners and participating countries permit installation.

A40-023.thesis: Existing AI services continue during the training pause using datacenters with mutually accepted inference-only verification.
A40-023.bar: Customers retain access to existing AI services during the pause, using datacenters that both governments accept as having functioning verification.
A40-023.actor: AI service providers and datacenter operators under US and Chinese verification.
indicatorsDecisive: Service availability records and bilateral inspector records show existing AI services operating from mutually verified datacenters throughout the pause.
indicatorsSupporting: Provider status reports document service availability during the pause.
Verified datacenter inventories show inference capacity coming online.
Customer usage and revenue reports show continued use of existing models.
indicatorsNo: Provider and verification records show existing AI services broadly cease for the duration of the training pause.
A40-023.condition: The US and China agree to pause new training and put mutually accepted inference-only verification in place.

A40-024.thesis: Most of the world joins the US–China AI agreement as it becomes the Consortium.
A40-024.bar: By the end of 2029, participation extends beyond the US and China to most of the world. The essay does not define whether this is measured by country count, population, or economic weight.
A40-024.actor: National governments outside the United States and China.
A40-024.measure: Countries joining the Consortium; the essay does not specify a numerical denominator
A40-024.window: By the end of the year
indicatorsDecisive: Official accession records show a majority of countries representing a majority of world population and economic output have joined the Consortium by the end of 2029.
indicatorsSupporting: Official treaty depositary records show additional countries signing or ratifying.
Major semiconductor supply-chain governments issue implementation rules.
Participating countries publish compute declarations.
indicatorsNo: Official treaty records show participation remains confined to the US, China, and a small minority of other countries at the end of 2029.
A40-024.condition: The US and China first reach a bilateral AI slowdown agreement and invite other countries to join.

A40-025.thesis: Public research transparency enables outside companies and auditors to detect and flag dangerous frontier AI work.
A40-025.bar: The transparency regime gives outsiders sufficient access to identify dangerous AI research and publicly or formally flag it; the claim does not require every dangerous activity to be detected.
A40-025.actor: Rival AI companies and independent auditors observing frontier AI developers' research.
indicatorsDecisive: A documented independent audit traces an identified dangerous frontier research practice to transparent research records and shows outsiders raising an alarm.
indicatorsSupporting: Public research databases contain detailed frontier training and experiment records.
Third-party auditors report access to current frontier research.
Independent researchers publish risk assessments based on disclosed research.
indicatorsNo: Audits show outsiders cannot access enough substantive frontier research to identify dangerous work, and documented dangerous work remains opaque to them.
A40-025.condition: The Consortium implements and maintains near-total public transparency for AI research after the US–China agreement.

A40-026.thesis: Dozens of companies in multiple countries reach the AI capability frontier under the deal.
A40-026.bar: At least dozens of distinct companies across multiple countries reach the contemporary frontier of AI capabilities; merely using another company's frontier service is not enough to establish that a company has caught up.
A40-026.actor: Dozens of AI companies across multiple countries, including leading US and Chinese AI labs and other companies.
A40-026.measure: Number of distinct companies with frontier-level AI capability
indicatorsDecisive: Independent cross-company evaluations and model-development records identify at least two dozen distinct companies in multiple countries with models at the contemporary frontier.
indicatorsSupporting: Benchmark leaderboards show a growing number of distinct model developers near the frontier.
Company technical reports document independently developed competitive frontier models.
Research disclosures show algorithmic advances spreading to additional companies.
indicatorsNo: Independent evaluations and developer records show fewer than two dozen companies reaching frontier capability throughout the 2030s.
A40-026.condition: The Consortium implements research transparency and slows frontier progress while allowing broad AI development and deployment.

A40-027.thesis: Open research reduces frontier companies' ability to maintain secret algorithmic advantages over competitors.
A40-027.bar: Compared with the pre-deal position, frontier firms can retain fewer or shorter-lived secret algorithmic advantages because their research discoveries are disclosed.
A40-027.actor: Frontier AI companies participating in the Consortium's research-transparency regime.
A40-027.target: A reduction from the pre-transparency level; no numerical magnitude specified
A40-027.measure: Extent and persistence of undisclosed algorithmic advantages among frontier AI companies
indicatorsDecisive: Comparative independent audits of pre-deal and post-deal frontier research show a reduction in the prevalence or duration of material secret algorithmic advantages attributable to disclosure.
indicatorsSupporting: Public research records show frontier algorithmic discoveries disclosed promptly.
Independent replication studies document competitors adopting disclosed methods.
Company technical reports show convergence in published training methods.
indicatorsNo: Audits show material secret algorithmic advantages remain as prevalent and persistent as before the deal despite the transparency regime.
A40-027.condition: The Consortium implements and continues public transparency for frontier AI research.

A40-028.thesis: Companies collectively operate 60 million AI agents continuously in 2032.
A40-028.bar: At a point in 2032, companies collectively run at least 60 million AI agent instances continuously. The separate speed and labor-output claims are not required here.
A40-028.actor: A variety of AI companies operating agents across the scenario's economy.
A40-028.measure: Number of continuously running AI agent instances across companies
indicatorsDecisive: Audited provider deployment inventories and independent industry estimates establish at least 60 million concurrently and continuously running AI agents.
indicatorsSupporting: Provider usage reports show rising concurrent agent-instance counts.
Datacenter inference capacity and utilization records support large continuous deployments.
Enterprise deployment surveys show growing use of persistent agents.
indicatorsNo: Comprehensive audited deployment estimates show fewer than 60 million continuously running agents throughout 2032.
A40-028.condition: A verified US–China agreement is implemented with broad participation, and Plan A continues to permit AI deployment through 2032.

A40-029.thesis: The continuously operating AI agents in the 2032 scenario run at about 20 times human speed.
A40-029.bar: The agents achieve at least 20 times the relevant human professional's speed on comparable cognitive work. The essay warns that speed varies by task and that token rate alone is not equivalent to useful work.
A40-029.actor: The AI agents operated across a variety of companies.
A40-029.measure: AI agent operating speed relative to human speed
indicatorsDecisive: Representative timed evaluations of the deployed agent population show at least 20× human-professional speed on comparable cognitive work, accounting for successful completion and operational delays.
indicatorsSupporting: METR 50% and 80% task horizons, with model and date, show improvement on autonomous work.
Timed professional-task benchmarks show large agent speed advantages.
Deployment telemetry reports high inference throughput and completed work volumes.
indicatorsNo: Representative timed comparisons show the deployed agents achieve less than 20× human-professional speed on comparable work throughout 2032.
A40-029.condition: A verified US–China agreement is implemented with broad participation and Plan A continues to permit the relevant agent deployments through 2032.

A40-030.thesis: US AI agents perform more cognitive labor than all humans combined, equivalent to about three billion human workers.
A40-030.bar: US AI agents collectively perform more cognitive labor than all humans combined and supply at least about three billion human-worker equivalents, accounting for speed, time worked, and effectiveness.
A40-030.actor: AI agents deployed by US companies and their human workforce comparison.
A40-030.target: More than all human cognitive labor; around 3 billion human-equivalent workers
A40-030.measure: US AI cognitive labor output in human-worker equivalents
indicatorsDecisive: A representative task-weighted accounting of deployed US AI output, calibrated to human worker productivity and hours, estimates at least three billion human-worker equivalents and more cognitive labor than humans collectively perform.
indicatorsSupporting: Provider and enterprise records show large numbers of deployed agents and their hours of operation.
Timed cognitive-task evaluations estimate AI output per human worker equivalent.
BLS occupational employment and hours data provide the human labor comparison.
indicatorsNo: A comprehensive task-weighted estimate places US AI cognitive output below three billion human-worker equivalents or below total human cognitive labor throughout 2032.
A40-030.condition: A verified US–China agreement is implemented with broad participation and Plan A continues through 2032.

A40-031.thesis: AI-driven growth raises US real GDP by about 50% in 2032.
A40-031.bar: BEA-consistent US real GDP rises by about 50% from 2031 to 2032, with credible analysis linking the growth to AI and robotics. The essay notes substantial measurement difficulty from changing relative prices and consumption baskets.
A40-031.actor: The US economy, with AI, robotics, firms, and workers contributing to output.
A40-031.target: 50% real GDP growth over one year
A40-031.measure: US real GDP growth from 2031 to 2032
indicatorsDecisive: BEA annual real GDP estimates show 2032 output at least 50% above 2031, supported by credible analysis of AI and robotics' contribution.
indicatorsSupporting: BEA quarterly real GDP data show accelerating output during 2032.
BEA investment and productivity accounts show rapid growth in AI and robot-intensive production.
Alternative price-indexed output estimates document the effect of changing consumption baskets.
indicatorsNo: BEA annual real GDP estimates and credible alternative deflators show 2032 growth materially below 50%.
A40-031.condition: A verified US–China agreement is implemented with broad participation and Plan A continues through 2032.

A40-032.thesis: Physical labor becomes the main bottleneck on construction and expansion in the 2032 AI-driven economy.
A40-032.bar: Abundant AI-produced ideas and designs cannot be built as quickly primarily because the available physical workforce constrains actual construction.
A40-032.actor: US construction and industrial firms and their physical workforce.
indicatorsDecisive: Construction-sector production and project analyses identify physical labor availability as the dominant constraint on converting available designs into completed capacity across the economy.
indicatorsSupporting: BLS JOLTS construction vacancies and wage data show exceptional demand for physical workers.
Project schedules cite workforce shortages as a cause of construction delays.
Investment filings show rapid expansion of robotics supply-chain capacity.
indicatorsNo: Representative project and production analyses identify other inputs, rather than physical labor, as the dominant constraint on construction expansion.
A40-032.condition: A verified US–China agreement is implemented with broad participation and Plan A continues through 2032.

A40-033.thesis: The United States begins an equal adult citizen's dividend at $45,000 per person per year in 2032.
A40-033.bar: A US dividend begins in 2032 and pays American adults equally at an annualized rate of at least $45,000 per person in 2025 dollars. The text describes adults, while its implementation footnote specifies citizens.
A40-033.actor: The US federal government and its Compute Dividend Corporation; eligible American adults receive the payments.
A40-033.target: $45,000 per adult per year, real 2025 dollars
A40-033.measure: Annual equal US citizen's dividend per eligible adult
indicatorsDecisive: Enacted US law and Treasury or dividend-corporation payment records establish an equal adult citizen dividend starting in 2032 at an annual rate of at least $45,000 in 2025 dollars.
indicatorsSupporting: Official budget legislation establishes a dividend fund.
Permit-auction receipts supply revenue for the program.
Treasury reports document enrollment and initial distributions.
indicatorsNo: Official payment records show no such dividend begins in 2032, or its annualized per-adult payment is below $45,000 in 2025 dollars.
A40-033.condition: The verified US–China agreement continues, and the US establishes the robot and compute permit system that funds the dividend.

A40-034.thesis: AI and robots perform about 20% of US economic labor in 2032, weighted by economic value.
A40-034.bar: AI and robots perform at least about 20% of US labor output when tasks are weighted by their economic value, rather than merely being capable of performing 20% of task types.
A40-034.actor: AI systems and robots performing work in the US economy.
A40-034.measure: AI and robot share of US labor output, weighted by economic value
indicatorsDecisive: A representative US task-output accounting, weighted by economic value and distinguishing actual machine work from human work, estimates an AI and robot share of at least 20%.
indicatorsSupporting: Enterprise task surveys measure AI and robot work performed across industries.
BLS occupational and wage data supply weights and human labor comparisons.
Deployment and production records show increased AI and robot operating hours.
indicatorsNo: A representative value-weighted accounting puts the actual AI and robot labor share below 20% throughout 2032.
A40-034.condition: A verified US–China agreement is implemented with broad participation and Plan A continues through 2032.

A40-035.thesis: The US adult citizen's dividend rises to about $1 million per person per year by 2035.
A40-035.bar: By the end of 2035, the equal US adult citizen's dividend reaches an annual rate of at least $1 million per person in 2025 dollars.
A40-035.actor: The US federal government and its Compute Dividend Corporation; eligible American adults receive the payments.
A40-035.target: $1 million per adult per year, real 2025 dollars
A40-035.measure: Annual equal US citizen's dividend per eligible adult
indicatorsDecisive: Treasury or dividend-corporation payment records establish an equal adult citizen dividend at an annual rate of at least $1 million in 2025 dollars by 2035.
indicatorsSupporting: Federal permit-auction receipts grow sufficiently to fund large distributions.
Dividend-corporation reports show increasing per-person payments.
Federal budget documents appropriate or allocate permit revenue to the dividend.
indicatorsNo: Official records show no eligible dividend or an annualized payment below $1 million in 2025 dollars through 2035.
A40-035.condition: The verified US–China agreement continues, and the US establishes and maintains the permit-funded citizen's dividend.

A40-036.thesis: AI and robots perform about 85% of US economic labor in 2035, weighted by economic value.
A40-036.bar: AI and robots actually perform at least about 85% of US labor output weighted by economic value. The relevant measure is not simply the percentage of task types that can be automated.
A40-036.actor: AI systems and robots performing work in the US economy.
A40-036.measure: AI and robot share of US labor output, weighted by economic value
indicatorsDecisive: A representative US task-output accounting, weighted by economic value and distinguishing actual machine work from human work, estimates an AI and robot share of at least 85%.
indicatorsSupporting: Industry task surveys measure actual AI and robot work across sectors.
BLS occupational employment, hours, and wages provide the human labor comparison and economic weights.
Robot deployment and AI service records show extensive operating capacity.
indicatorsNo: A representative value-weighted accounting places the actual AI and robot labor share below 85% throughout 2035.
A40-036.condition: A verified US–China agreement is implemented with broad participation and Plan A continues through 2035.

A40-037.thesis: US robot and compute permit fees generate enough revenue to replace the declining labor-tax revenue base.
A40-037.bar: Robot and compute permit receipts are large enough to offset the decline in US federal revenue from personal income and payroll taxes as AI and robots displace labor. The claim concerns replacement capacity, not a requirement that all permit revenue be allocated to that purpose.
A40-037.actor: The US federal government, collecting fees from companies buying robot and compute permits.
A40-037.target: Permit revenue at least sufficient to replace lost labor-tax revenue; the scenario reports $50 trillion in FY2032
A40-037.measure: US federal robot and compute permit receipts compared with the decline in personal income and payroll tax revenue
A40-037.window: 2030s; the scenario gives FY2032 as an example
indicatorsDecisive: Treasury and permit-auction accounts show annual federal robot and compute permit receipts at least equal to the inflation-adjusted decline in personal income and payroll tax receipts from the relevant pre-decline baseline.
indicatorsSupporting: Official auction records show substantial robot and compute permit receipts.
Treasury revenue tables show the trajectory of personal income and payroll tax receipts.
BLS employment and earnings data show the labor-market changes affecting the tax base.
indicatorsNo: Federal accounts show permit receipts remain below the decline in personal income and payroll tax revenue throughout the 2030s.
A40-037.condition: The Consortium agrees to cap robot and compute production, and the United States implements a permit-auction system under the continuing agreement.

A40-038.thesis: World AI compute reaches 60 billion H100-equivalents at the beginning of 2034 under Plan A.
A40-038.bar: The worldwide stock of AI compute has at least 60 billion H100-equivalents of aggregate performance at the beginning of 2034.
A40-038.measure: Global stock of AI compute at the beginning of 2034, measured in H100-equivalent processing performance
indicatorsDecisive: A global inventory combining chip shipments, retirements and measured fp16 performance finds at least 60 billion H100-equivalents in AI compute at the start of 2034.
indicatorsSupporting: Epoch AI data-centre tracking and operator filings show rapid growth in installed AI capacity.
Nvidia, AMD, Google, Huawei and TSMC filings show sufficient AI chip production and shipments.
Utility filings and data-centre power inventories support the implied buildout.
indicatorsNo: A credible global inventory places AI compute materially below 60 billion H100-equivalents at the start of 2034.
A40-038.condition: The US and China sign an agreement in 2029, verification is implemented, most of the world joins the Consortium, and Plan A continues to be implemented through 2034.

A40-039.thesis: By 2034, about 99% of global fabrication capacity is in fabs built after the 2029 agreement.
A40-039.bar: About 99% of worldwide fab capacity in 2034 is capacity built after the agreement. Because this is a share, a materially lower or higher share is an error.
A40-039.measure: Share of worldwide fabrication capacity in facilities built after the 2029 deal
indicatorsDecisive: A capacity-weighted worldwide fab census with construction dates finds about 99% of capacity was built after the 2029 agreement.
indicatorsSupporting: Semiconductor industry capacity surveys document a large post-deal fab construction wave.
Operator filings and construction records show when major fabs came online.
Equipment supplier shipments show a large post-deal expansion of fabrication facilities.
indicatorsNo: A capacity-weighted global fab census finds a materially different share built after the deal.
A40-039.condition: The US and China sign an agreement in 2029, verification is implemented, most of the world joins the Consortium, and Plan A continues to be implemented through 2034.

A40-040.thesis: A credible mutually assured compute destruction arrangement continues to make the major powers' and middle powers' new compute rapidly destroyable if the deal breaks down.
A40-040.bar: In 2034 the shutdown and destruction arrangements give the relevant powers a credible, rapid means of preventing rivals from using the new compute if the deal collapses or war occurs. Actual deal dissolution is not necessary to demonstrate credibility.
A40-040.actor: The US and Chinese governments and militaries, and middle powers operating datacenters
indicatorsDecisive: Independent technical and military assessments establish that the deployed destruction arrangements would rapidly disable the relevant US, Chinese and middle-power compute despite plausible attempts to seize or defend it.
indicatorsSupporting: Official agreements and inspection records document reciprocal destruction rights and deployment of shutdown mechanisms.
Facility locations, troop deployments and tested chip destruction systems support the deterrent.
Independent exercises demonstrate rapid disabling of representative sites.
indicatorsNo: A credible security assessment establishes that a major power can retain and use substantial new compute despite the destruction arrangements.
A deal breakdown or war occurs and the relevant new compute remains usable by its owner or a rival.
A40-040.condition: The US and China sign an agreement in 2029, verification is implemented, most of the world joins the Consortium, and the compute destruction arrangements remain in operation through 2034.

A40-041.thesis: The most capable AIs reach top-human-expert performance across fields by 2035.
A40-041.bar: The most capable systems equal or exceed top human experts across cognitive fields, subject to the author's exceptions for capabilities not yet trained and inherently human tasks. A few strong benchmark results alone are insufficient.
A40-041.actor: Developers of the most powerful AI systems worldwide
A40-041.measure: AI performance versus top human experts across cognitive fields
indicatorsDecisive: A broad independent evaluation spanning cognitive fields and real professional tasks finds frontier systems at or above published top-human-expert baselines across the relevant trained capabilities.
indicatorsSupporting: Benchmark authors report frontier-model results exceeding their published expert baselines in multiple fields.
Independent studies find expert-level performance on extended, real professional assignments.
Deployment records show experts using frontier AIs for demanding work in many professions.
indicatorsNo: Broad independent evaluations reveal substantial trained cognitive fields where the strongest systems remain below top human experts.
A40-041.condition: The US and China sign an agreement in 2029, verification is implemented, most of the world joins the Consortium, and Plan A continues to be implemented through 2035.

A40-042.thesis: Cross-company AI monitoring, embedded in a broader control system, prevents even adversarially misaligned AIs from subverting or escaping human control.
A40-042.bar: A deployed, cross-company monitoring and defense system provides robust control over the relevant frontier AIs even when they try to evade it; evidence of a few caught incidents alone does not establish this.
A40-042.actor: Frontier AI companies, their monitoring systems and regulators
indicatorsDecisive: Independent audits and adversarial evaluations establish that the deployed cross-company monitoring and associated barriers prevent relevant frontier AIs from escaping or subverting human control across credible attack paths.
indicatorsSupporting: Regulatory records require monitoring by independently trained models from different providers.
Red-team reports document detection and repair of attempted collusion and escape strategies.
Incident logs show monitors flagging suspicious frontier-model behavior in deployment.
indicatorsNo: A frontier AI escapes monitoring or gains unapproved control despite the deployed defenses.
Independent testing exposes a credible unpatched route for frontier AIs to subvert the control system.
A40-042.condition: The US and China sign an agreement in 2029, verification is implemented, most of the world joins the Consortium, and Plan A's cross-company monitoring and control regime is deployed.

A40-043.thesis: Control-based safety cases cease to be sufficient around top-expert capability, so scaling substantially beyond that level requires alignment-based trust.
A40-043.bar: At approximately top-expert capability, control alone can no longer provide high confidence against catastrophic harm from deliberately adversarial, more capable AIs; a substantially superhuman transition therefore requires trust in alignment.
A40-043.actor: AI developers, safety researchers and regulators
A40-043.window: At the top-human-expert threshold, reached in the scenario in 2035
indicatorsDecisive: Independently reviewed safety analyses and adversarial tests establish that available control measures cannot give high confidence against catastrophic behavior above approximately top-expert capability, while alignment-based assurance is needed to scale further.
indicatorsSupporting: Red-team evaluations show increasingly capable AIs bypassing proposed monitoring or containment.
Published safety cases show human auditors unable to evaluate the arguments needed for substantially stronger systems.
Regulatory decisions pause capability scaling at the level supported by control-based cases.
indicatorsNo: A robust, independently validated control system provides high confidence against catastrophic behavior by substantially superhuman adversarial AIs without relying on their alignment.
Control-based assurance fails materially below the top-expert region rather than around it.
A40-043.condition: The US and China sign an agreement in 2029, verification is implemented, most of the world joins the Consortium, and regulated frontier AI reaches top-expert capability.

A40-044.thesis: Mechanistic interpretability becomes significantly better than observing behavior alone for identifying AI honesty and deception.
A40-044.bar: By 2035, researchers can often distinguish honesty from lying using internal model evidence, with a significant advantage over common-sense observation of behavior.
indicatorsDecisive: Blinded, independently replicated evaluations with known ground truth show interpretability methods often identifying deception and significantly outperforming behavioral observation on comparable cases.
indicatorsSupporting: Published studies identify internal representations associated with deception in several models.
Prospective interpretability analyses flag previously unknown deceptive behavior later confirmed by independent investigation.
Research teams deploy internal-state analysis alongside behavioral monitoring.
indicatorsNo: Well-powered comparative evaluations show interpretability performs no better than behavioral observation at detecting deception.
Interpretability methods cannot reliably identify honesty or lying beyond isolated demonstrations.
A40-044.condition: The US and China sign an agreement in 2029, verification is implemented, most of the world joins the Consortium, and Plan A's alignment research continues through 2035.

A40-045.thesis: Retrospective interpretability audits reveal previously unrecognized misalignment, sabotage and escape attempts in early-2030s AI logs.
A40-045.bar: Retrospective analyses of early-2030s logs disclose many previously unrecognized misalignment examples, including sabotage and at least a few attempts to escape control.
A40-045.actor: AI safety researchers and their AI interpretability systems
indicatorsDecisive: Audited incident reports identify many previously unknown early-2030s misalignment cases, including documented sabotage and multiple escape attempts discovered through retrospective interpretability analysis.
indicatorsSupporting: Labs retain and release early-2030s model activity logs for retrospective analysis.
Investigations verify a previously unknown case of model sabotage.
Interpretability research identifies suspicious internal activity associated with attempted evasion.
indicatorsNo: Comprehensive retrospective audits find no previously unknown sabotage or escape attempts in the relevant logs.
Purported discoveries are shown to be artifacts rather than actual earlier AI behavior.
A40-045.condition: The US and China sign an agreement in 2029, verification is implemented, most of the world joins the Consortium, and relevant AI logs and interpretability tools are available for retrospective analysis.

A40-046.thesis: The global active frontier-AI population averages about 200 million instances in early 2036.
A40-046.bar: In early 2036 the average number of active frontier AI instances worldwide reaches about 200 million; exceeding that number counts as meeting the point target.
A40-046.actor: Operators of frontier AI systems worldwide
A40-046.target: 200 million average active frontier AI instances
A40-046.measure: Average number of running frontier-model instances worldwide, accounting for instances being turned on and off and agent scaffolding
indicatorsDecisive: A credible global compute and deployment inventory estimates at least 200 million concurrently active frontier-model instances on average in early 2036.
indicatorsSupporting: Frontier providers publish instance-hours and average concurrency figures.
Data-centre inventories show enough inference capacity to support the implied population.
Enterprise and public deployment reports document rapid growth in frontier-agent use.
indicatorsNo: A credible global inventory finds materially fewer than 200 million average active frontier AI instances in early 2036.
A40-046.condition: The US and China sign an agreement in 2029, verification is implemented, most of the world joins the Consortium, and Plan A continues to be implemented into early 2036.

A40-047.thesis: The worldwide robot population reaches about two billion in early 2036.
A40-047.bar: The global stock reaches about two billion individual robots in early 2036; exceeding the point target counts as meeting it. Human-equivalent labor is not the count.
A40-047.measure: Worldwide stock of individual robots, including humanoid and specialized form factors
indicatorsDecisive: A global robot stock census finds at least two billion individual robots across relevant form factors in early 2036.
indicatorsSupporting: Robot manufacturers' production and delivery filings show cumulative shipments consistent with a two-billion stock.
Industrial and service robot inventories show rapid deployment across countries.
Supply-chain reports show corresponding growth in robot components and assembly capacity.
indicatorsNo: A credible global stock census finds materially fewer than two billion robots in early 2036.
A40-047.condition: The US and China sign an agreement in 2029, verification is implemented, most of the world joins the Consortium, and Plan A continues to be implemented into early 2036.

A40-048.thesis: As AI and robotics transform the economy, the US employment rate falls to 26% in 2036.
A40-048.bar: The US employment-to-population rate is about 26% in 2036. This is an explicitly low share, so a materially higher rate misses the claim; a materially lower rate also differs from the stated point.
A40-048.actor: The US population and labor market
A40-048.measure: US employment-to-population rate, using the employment-rate population convention underlying the scenario
indicatorsDecisive: BLS Current Population Survey employment-to-population data, with a denominator matched to the scenario, show about 26% employed in 2036.
indicatorsSupporting: BLS CES payroll employment falls substantially relative to population.
BLS JOLTS reports sustained changes in vacancies and hiring.
CPS labor-force participation and industry employment show widespread withdrawal from paid work.
indicatorsNo: BLS CPS data show an employment-to-population rate materially different from 26% in 2036.
A40-048.condition: The US and China sign an agreement in 2029, verification is implemented, most of the world joins the Consortium, and Plan A continues to be implemented through 2036.

A40-049.thesis: Industrial activity and new dense settlements are concentrated enough that about 99% of the world remains historic or nature preserves.
A40-049.bar: About 99% of world land is maintained as historic or nature preserves, with historic places broadly retaining their earlier appearance, as industrial zones and arcologies occupy the remainder.
A40-049.actor: Governments, landowners and industrial developers worldwide
A40-049.measure: Share of worldwide land in historic and nature preserves rather than industrial zones or new arcologies
indicatorsDecisive: A global land-use and remote-sensing inventory finds about 99% of land in historic or nature preserves, including historic settlements retaining broadly their earlier form.
indicatorsSupporting: Satellite land-cover data show the footprint of industrial zones and new arcologies.
National land-use inventories document preserved historic and natural areas.
Planning records show concentrated high-density construction and designated industrial zones.
indicatorsNo: Global land-use data show a materially different fraction of land preserved in the described sense.
Historic settlements and natural areas are extensively transformed rather than broadly preserved.
A40-049.condition: The US and China sign an agreement in 2029, verification is implemented, most of the world joins the Consortium, and Plan A continues to be implemented through 2036.

A40-050.thesis: Under the AI-driven abundance of the scenario, malnutrition, lack of medicine and homelessness become rare worldwide.
A40-050.bar: All three forms of deprivation are rare worldwide by 2036, not merely reduced in the United States. The author provides no numerical cutoff for 'nearly banished.'
A40-050.actor: Populations and health, housing and welfare systems worldwide
indicatorsDecisive: Credible global nutrition, access-to-medicines and homelessness datasets together show each condition has become rare across the world.
indicatorsSupporting: FAO and national nutrition surveys show steep declines in malnutrition.
WHO and national health surveys show improved access to essential medicines.
National housing censuses and homelessness counts fall sharply.
Income and food-price data show improved ability to afford necessities.
indicatorsNo: Global surveys show any one of malnutrition, lack of medicine or homelessness remains widespread in 2036.
A40-050.condition: The US and China sign an agreement in 2029, verification is implemented, most of the world joins the Consortium, and Plan A continues to be implemented through 2036.

A40-051.thesis: AI-assisted investigations and privacy-preserving audits become a normal means of scrutinizing politicians, improving political accountability.
A40-051.bar: Privacy-preserving AI inspection of politicians' data is a normal response to allegations, and credible evidence links the resulting scrutiny to somewhat improved conduct or constraints on politicians.
A40-051.actor: Politicians, voters and independent AI-auditing providers, especially in the US political setting
indicatorsDecisive: Representative political-practice data show routine use of independent privacy-preserving AI audits for allegations, and credible comparative research links their use to improved political conduct or accountability.
indicatorsSupporting: Election and ethics records document politicians submitting private records to independent AI auditors.
Third-party audit reports describe privacy-preserving procedures and disclosed findings.
Investigative records show previously concealed misconduct being revealed with AI assistance.
Surveys show voters expect or use audit results when evaluating politicians.
indicatorsNo: Political audits of the described kind remain exceptional rather than normal in 2037.
Credible evidence shows the audits do not improve accountability or politicians' conduct.
A40-051.condition: The US and China sign an agreement in 2029, verification is implemented, most of the world joins the Consortium, and Plan A continues through deployment of AI-assisted privacy-preserving auditing.

A40-052.thesis: AI-assisted technology makes useful human lie detection possible in the 2030s.
A40-052.bar: A human lie-detection method aided by AI works quite well in practice, demonstrated against known truths and lies. The author does not specify an accuracy threshold or rule out invasive scans.
A40-052.actor: Developers and users of human lie-detection technology
A40-052.window: 2037 in the scenario; within a few years of turbocharged AI labor
indicatorsDecisive: Independent, blinded, ecologically realistic studies with known ground truth demonstrate that an AI-assisted human lie detector works quite well across relevant users and statements.
indicatorsSupporting: Laboratory studies report improved discrimination of known truths and lies using AI-assisted measurements.
Independent teams replicate results on new participants.
Documented deployments use the method in real investigations with subsequent verification.
indicatorsNo: Independent, realistic validation finds proposed AI-assisted detectors perform poorly at distinguishing lies from truths.
No working AI-assisted human lie detector exists in the scenario window.
A40-052.condition: The US and China sign an agreement in 2029, verification is implemented, most of the world joins the Consortium, and AI-assisted research continues under Plan A.

A40-053.thesis: By 2038 researchers possess a mature, empirically supported science explaining and predicting how neural-network goals, drives and values form.
A40-053.bar: A mature theoretical and empirical discipline explains and predicts goal formation, with tested alternatives and direct interpretability evidence confirming its predictions across relevant systems.
indicatorsDecisive: An independently assessed research literature contains predictive theory, tested and rejected alternatives, and interpretability observations confirming the theory across relevant neural networks.
indicatorsSupporting: Textbooks synthesize a coherent theory of learned goals, drives and values.
Preregistered studies correctly predict how training changes model motivations.
Interpretability analyses identify internal features associated with predicted goals.
Training laboratories adopt theory-based protocols for multiple desired traits.
indicatorsNo: Predictions of leading goal-formation theories systematically fail independent tests.
The field still lacks an empirically supported general account of how neural-network goals form.
A40-053.condition: The US and China sign an agreement in 2029, verification is implemented, most of the world joins the Consortium, and alignment research continues under Plan A through 2038.

A40-054.thesis: Standard honesty-training protocols produce true honesty rather than merely behavior that passes tests.
A40-054.bar: A standard training protocol produces genuinely honest AIs, including in novel or adversarial circumstances, rather than systems that merely appear honest or deceive themselves.
indicatorsDecisive: Independent generalization studies and validated interpretability analyses together show that the standard protocol produces true honesty across novel and adversarial settings, excluding concealed lying and self-deception.
indicatorsSupporting: Published protocol evaluations show honest behavior on held-out tasks and incentives.
Interpretability studies find internal representations consistent with truthfulness.
Deployed systems volunteer adverse information that ordinary reward or reputation incentives would favor concealing.
indicatorsNo: A standard-protocol model is shown to systematically conceal lies or deceive itself in novel conditions.
Independent evaluations show honesty training fails to generalize beyond its test settings.
A40-054.condition: The US and China sign an agreement in 2029, verification is implemented, most of the world joins the Consortium, and alignment research continues under Plan A through 2038.

A40-055.thesis: The global pause near top-expert AI capability continues through 2039 despite substantial alignment progress.
A40-055.bar: After reaching roughly top-expert capability, the global frontier remains near that level through 2039 rather than scaling to generally superhuman AI, even as alignment improves. Minor progress consistent with the author's near-pause is allowed.
A40-055.actor: Consortium governments, regulators and frontier AI developers
indicatorsDecisive: Independent frontier evaluations and regulatory records show capability growth held near top-expert level through the end of 2039 while alignment methods improve.
indicatorsSupporting: Official Consortium and national rules retain control-based safety-case requirements through 2039.
Frontier-model benchmarks show only limited progress beyond the 2035 capability level.
Published safety research reports improved alignment during the pause.
indicatorsNo: A generally superhuman frontier AI is developed before the end of 2039.
The global capability pause is lifted and sustained scaling resumes before 2040.
A40-055.condition: The US and China sign an agreement in 2029, verification is implemented, most of the world joins the Consortium, and the Consortium reaches and maintains the top-expert pause.

A40-056.thesis: The US Citizen's Dividend reaches $10 million per recipient per year in 2039, measured in real 2025 dollars.
A40-056.bar: The annualized equal Citizen's Dividend reaches at least $10 million per eligible American recipient in real 2025 dollars during 2039. The main text's adult formulation and footnote's citizen formulation should be retained when identifying the actual recipient population.
A40-056.actor: The US government and its Compute Dividend Corporation
A40-056.target: $10 million per year per recipient, in 2025 dollars
A40-056.measure: Annual equal US Citizen's Dividend payment per eligible recipient
indicatorsDecisive: Official dividend payment records show annual payments of at least $10 million in 2025 dollars per eligible recipient in 2039.
indicatorsSupporting: Federal budget and Compute Dividend Corporation filings show sufficient permit revenue allocated to dividends.
Treasury payment records show rapid growth in per-recipient distributions.
Census recipient counts and audited fund accounts support the per-person calculation.
indicatorsNo: Official records show the annual dividend materially below $10 million in 2025 dollars per eligible recipient in 2039.
No comparable US Citizen's Dividend exists in 2039.
A40-056.condition: The US and China sign an agreement in 2029, verification is implemented, most of the world joins the Consortium, and the US establishes and continues the permit-funded Citizen's Dividend through 2039.

A40-058.thesis: After the managed top-expert pause, AI systems reach superintelligence in 2040.
A40-058.bar: Following the pause, at least one AI system is significantly better than the best humans at everything, while also being faster and cheaper, in 2040. Top-expert performance in selected fields is insufficient.
A40-058.actor: Frontier AI developers operating under the Consortium's regulatory arrangements
indicatorsDecisive: Comprehensive independent evaluations and cost and speed measurements establish that a system significantly exceeds the best humans across the relevant full range of tasks while operating faster and cheaper.
indicatorsSupporting: Benchmark results exceed published best-human baselines across a wide range of domains.
Frontier deployment records demonstrate sustained, faster-than-human performance on complex novel tasks.
