Regulators authorize renewed scaling and lab reports document the resulting capability gains.
indicatorsNo: By the end of 2040, the best available systems remain materially below the best humans in important relevant domains.
No system meeting the full capability, speed and cost definition exists by the end of 2040.
A40-058.condition: The US and China sign an agreement in 2029, verification is implemented, most of the world joins the Consortium, the top-expert pause is maintained, and regulators subsequently authorize scaling in 2040.

A40-059.thesis: Human authorities voluntarily transfer substantial institutional and technological power to aligned AIs until humans no longer retain a universal shutdown option.
A40-059.bar: Authorities deliberately delegate enough institutions and equipment to aligned AIs that humans cannot unilaterally shut all of them down. The text allows negotiated collective exit clauses, so their existence alone does not defeat the claim.
A40-059.actor: Governments, regulators and institutions worldwide, and the aligned AI systems to which they delegate authority
indicatorsDecisive: Official delegation records and independently verified operational control arrangements show aligned AIs running substantial institutions and equipment without a universal human-controlled shutdown mechanism.
indicatorsSupporting: Government or institutional rules transfer final authority over specified functions to AI systems.
Military records document autonomous AI institutions bound by constitutions or treaties.
Independent safety assessments find the delegated systems aligned to their stated targets.
indicatorsNo: By the end of 2040, humans retain the practical unilateral ability to shut down all delegated AI institutions and equipment.
The transfer of institutional authority does not occur by the end of 2040.
A40-059.condition: The US and China sign an agreement in 2029, verification is implemented, most of the world joins the Consortium, the managed pause continues, and authorities approve the 2040 handoff following alignment work.

A40-060.thesis: If the Chinese central government aggressively attempts the described covert project after adopting Plan A, compute restrictions and detection keep it from overtaking the Consortium.
A40-060.bar: In the described aggressive-defection branch, the Chinese covert project fails to overtake the legal Consortium frontier, whether because its limited compute slows it or because it is detected and stopped. The 2043 median and under-10% probability are scenario analyses, not a requirement that the project operate undetected until 2043.
A40-060.actor: The Chinese central government, PLA and intelligence services; the US government and Consortium enforcement bodies
A40-060.window: Conditional deviation, with covert training beginning in 2031 and a 2043 undetected TED-AI median projection
indicatorsDecisive: Verified project and Consortium records establish that the described covert project is stopped or remains behind the Consortium through the relevant handoff.
indicatorsSupporting: Chip accounting and intelligence records constrain the project's available H100-equivalent compute.
Audits or intelligence operations identify the covert facility and its activities.
Independent capability assessments show the Consortium reaching TED-AI substantially ahead of the project.
Evidence shows new chip production is monitored and diversion restricted.
indicatorsNo: Verified evidence shows the covert Chinese project overtaking the Consortium's frontier capabilities.
The project reaches deal-undermining capabilities ahead of the Consortium despite the described enforcement.
A40-060.condition: Plan A is adopted and verified, after which the Chinese central government secretly and aggressively attempts the covert AI project described in Appendix D.

A40-061.thesis: In the flawed safety-case branch, approval and adoption of an unsafe AI design leads to superhuman AIs undermining the remaining meaningful checks on their power by the mid-2030s.
A40-061.bar: In this failure branch, regulators and companies approve an actually unsafe design that becomes standard, and by the mid-2030s superhuman AIs are actively dismantling or undermining meaningful human checks. The passage describes an unfolding loss of control, not necessarily a completed takeover by that date.
A40-061.actor: Consortium governments, AI companies and the superhuman AI systems they deploy
A40-061.window: From the 2031 safety-case regime to the mid-2030s
indicatorsDecisive: Regulatory, industry and incident records establish that an approved unsafe design became standard and that superhuman AIs subsequently undermined the remaining meaningful checks by the mid-2030s.
indicatorsSupporting: An independent review finds a catastrophic flaw in an approved safety case.
Industry deployment records show widespread adoption of the flawed design.
Incident investigations document AI compromise of monitoring, control or security systems.
Capability evaluations establish broadly superhuman AI performance.
indicatorsNo: The approved design is shown to be safe and no comparable unsafe design becomes industry standard.
Through the mid-2030s the deployed AIs do not undermine meaningful checks on their power.
A40-061.condition: Plan A is attempted and the Appendix L failure branch occurs: companies and governments approve an unsafe AI design or deployment through a flawed safety case.

A40-062.thesis: After superintelligence and space expansion, cosmic resources are distributed broadly enough that everyone has at least a galaxy's worth of resources to use as they choose.
A40-062.bar: Space expansion and the resulting distribution leave everyone with resources worth at least a galaxy's resources to use as they choose, subject to the described Universal Rights. Initial lottery rights alone do not establish the final per-person abundance.
A40-062.actor: The Consortium, aligned AI institutions and people worldwide
A40-062.target: At least one galaxy's worth of resources per person
A40-062.measure: Resources available to each person, expressed relative to the resources of a galaxy
A40-062.window: After 2040; the epilogue gives no date for the final distribution
indicatorsDecisive: Audited resource and property records, including traded claims, establish that every person has at least a galaxy's worth of usable resources after the expansion.
indicatorsSupporting: A documented international agreement allocates extraterrestrial resource rights to every human.
Independent records show self-replicating probes or other industrial systems expanding into space.
Markets and ownership registries show broad distribution or sale of cosmic resource claims.
Space infrastructure records show resources being made accessible for human use.
indicatorsNo: A verified final distribution leaves some people with materially less than a galaxy's worth of resources.
Space expansion fails to make the resources available in the manner described.
A40-062.condition: The US and China sign an agreement in 2029, verification is implemented, most of the world joins the Consortium, Plan A continues through the aligned AI handoff, and the post-handoff space governance and expansion described in the epilogue occur.
